+def critical_single_layer_partition(layer: int, renewal: list[float]) -> float:
+    """Evaluate the exact one-layer critical partition function from u_j."""
+    if layer < 1 or layer >= len(renewal):
+        raise ValueError("renewal coefficients must be available through layer")
+    return 2.0 * sum(renewal[:layer]) + renewal[layer] - 1.0
+
+
+def single_layer_orbit_counter(
+    layer: int, generators: list[Counter[int]]
+) -> Counter[int]:
+    """Recover the standard Fibonacci-partition spectrum on one layer."""
+    if layer < 1 or layer >= len(generators):
+        raise ValueError("generator table must include costs through layer")
+    levels: Counter[int] = Counter({1: 1})
+    for cost in range(1, layer + 1):
+        orbit_weight = 2 if cost < layer else 1
+        for level, word_count in generators[cost].items():
+            levels[level] += orbit_weight * word_count
+    return levels
+

+\section{Thermodynamics of the Fibonacci partition function}
+\label{sec:standard-thermodynamics}
+
+The renewal identity was derived from Weinstein's standard Fibonacci
+partition function before it was transferred to the finite-window fold.  We
+now state its one-layer consequences intrinsically.  This removes the bespoke
+fold from the probabilistic conclusions.
+
+For \(m\ge1\), recall
+\[
+ \mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1)
+\]
+and define
+\[
+ Z_m^R(t):=\sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^t
+ \qquad(t\in\RR).
+\]
+If \(\mathbf N_m\) is uniform on \(\mathcal I_m\), put
+\[
+ Y_m^R:=\frac1m\log R(\mathbf N_m).
+\]
+
+\begin{theorem}[One-layer Fibonacci partition thermodynamics]
+\label{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics}
+For every \(t\in\RR\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log Z_m^R(t)=P(t),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-pressure}
+\end{equation}
+where \(P\) is the pressure in \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure}.  Thus the
+one-layer pressure is zero on \((-\infty,-\sigma_0]\), is positive, real
+analytic, and strictly convex on \((-\sigma_0,\infty)\), and has the
+one-sided derivatives in \eqref{eq:critical-pressure-slopes}.
+
+For \(s>\sigma_0\), the unnormalized sums satisfy
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-s)\longrightarrow
+ \mathcal Z_R(s):=
+ \frac2{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-1.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-frozen-limit}
+\end{equation}
+At the critical tilt,
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)\sim\frac{2m}{\mu_C}.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}
+\end{equation}
+
+For \(n\in\mathcal I_m\) with \(R(n)>2\), let \(g(n)\) be the generating
+number of its Weinstein orbit and put \(\ell_m^R(n)=L(g(n))\); set
+\(\ell_m^R(n)=0\) when \(R(n)\le2\).  Let \(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m\) have the
+critical Gibbs law
+\[
+ \Pr\{\widehat{\mathbf N}_m=n\}
+ =\frac{R(n)^{-\sigma_0}}{Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)}
+ \qquad(n\in\mathcal I_m).
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}
+ \left(
+  \frac1m\log R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m),
+  \frac1m\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)
+ \right)
+ \xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{\mathrm d}(v_cU,U),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-gibbs}
+\end{equation}
+where \(U\) is uniform on \([0,1]\).
+
+Finally, \((Y_m^R)\) satisfies a full large deviation principle with speed
+\(m\) and the good rate function
+\begin{equation}
+ I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}
+ \{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-ldp-rate}
+\end{equation}
+Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), where
+\(\alpha_+=\tfrac12\log\varphi\), and
+\[
+ I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
+ \qquad(0\le\alpha\le v_c).
+\]
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put \(H_m(s)=\sum_{j=0}^m u_j(s)\).  The exact one-layer renewal identity
+\eqref{eq:weighted-layer-renewal} says
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-s)=2H_{m-1}(s)+u_m(s)-1.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-renewal}
+\end{equation}
+The proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} established
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log u_m(s)
+ =\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log H_m(s)
+ =P(-s).
+\]
+Since \(u_m(s)\le Z_m^R(-s)\le3H_m(s)\), this proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure}.
+
+If \(s>\sigma_0\), then \(U_s(1)=\sum_{j\ge0}u_j(s)<\infty\), so
+\(u_m(s)\to0\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-generating-function} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} give
+\[
+ U_s(1)=\frac1{1-B_s(1)}
+ =\frac1{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}.
+\]
+Letting \(m\to\infty\) in \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-frozen-limit}.  At \(s=\sigma_0\), the arithmetic
+renewal theorem used in \Cref{thm:critical-finite-window-gibbs} gives
+\(u_m(\sigma_0)\to1/\mu_C\).  Ces\`aro summation in
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}.
+
+We next retain the generating cost.  The four orbit branches displayed above
+\eqref{eq:marked-microcanonical-count} show that a generator of cost \(c\)
+contributes two points to \(\mathcal I_m\) if \(c<m\), one if \(c=m\), and
+none if \(c>m\).  Thus the one-layer boundary weight is
+\[
+ K_m^R(c)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  2,&c<m,\\
+  1,&c=m,\\
+  0,&c>m.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+With the marked renewal measure \(\mathcal U\) defined before
+\eqref{eq:marked-microcanonical-count}, the same free-monoid bijection gives,
+for every Borel set
+\(B\subset\mathbb R\times(\log2,\infty)\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \card{\{n\in\mathcal I_m:
+   (\ell_m^R(n),\log R(n))\in B\}}
+ =\int_B K_m^R(c)e^{\sigma_0h}\,\mathcal U(dc,dh).
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-marked-count}
+\end{equation}
+The points with \(R(n)\le2\) have bounded total critical weight, uniformly in
+\(m\), by the uniform layer-count lemma.
+
+For every bounded continuous \(f\) on \([0,1]\), the arithmetic renewal
+theorem and a Riemann-sum argument give
+\[
+ \frac1m\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_j(\sigma_0)f(j/m)
+ \longrightarrow\frac1{\mu_C}\int_0^1f(y)\,dy.
+\]
+After multiplication of \eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} by
+\(e^{-\sigma_0h}\), the weights are two for \(j<m\) and one at \(j=m\).
+Together with \eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}, this proves
+\[
+ \frac{\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)}m
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}U.
+\]
+For the reward coordinate, the critical renewal increments
+\((C_i,H_i)\) satisfy
+\[
+ \frac{H_1+\cdots+H_r}{C_1+\cdots+C_r}
+ \longrightarrow\frac{\mu_H}{\mu_C}=v_c
+\quad\text{almost surely}.
+\]
+Every cost increment is at least three.  Consequently the number of renewal
+epochs with total cost at most \(m\) and reward-to-cost ratio outside a fixed
+\(\delta\)-neighborhood of \(v_c\) is \(o(m)\), pathwise and, by bounded
+convergence after division by \(m\), in expectation.  Since \(K_m^R\le2\),
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} and
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size} imply
+\[
+ \frac1m\log R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)
+ -v_c\frac{\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)}m
+ \xrightarrow{\Pr}0.
+\]
+This proves \eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-gibbs}.
+
+It remains to prove the full LDP, in particular the lower bound at the
+nonexposed slopes.  The layer has
+\(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\), and hence
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log\card{\mathcal I_m}=\log\varphi.
+\]
+Equation \eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure} therefore gives the limiting
+logarithmic moment generating function
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m
+ \log\mathbb E e^{tmY_m^R}=P(t)-\log\varphi.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-log-mgf}
+\]
+The translated extremal theorem in the Fibonacci-convention lemma gives
+\[
+ \max_{n\in\mathcal I_m}\frac1m\log R(n)
+ \longrightarrow\alpha_+.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-maximum}
+\]
+Indeed, the two shifted endpoints have partition value one, so they do not
+change the maximum on the intervening Fibonacci block.  Thus the variables
+are exponentially tight, and the G\"artner--Ellis upper bound gives the
+required upper bound for closed sets.
+
+For the lower bound, fix \(t>t_c=-\sigma_0\), write \(v=P'(t)>v_c\), and
+tilt the uniform law on \(\mathcal I_n\) by \(R(k)^t\).  Analyticity of \(P\)
+and the exponential Markov inequality applied to
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure} show that this tilted law assigns
+exponentially vanishing mass to
+\[
+ \left\{k\in\mathcal I_n:
+   \left|n^{-1}\log R(k)-v\right|\ge\delta\right\}.
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ A_n^R(v,\delta)
+ :=\card{\{k\in\mathcal I_n:
+ |n^{-1}\log R(k)-v|<\delta\}},
+\]
+then
+\begin{equation}
+ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log A_n^R(v,\delta)
+ \ge P(t)-tv-|t|\delta.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}
+\end{equation}
+
+For large \(n\), every point counted here has multiplicity greater than two.
+Each generating orbit contributes at most two points to \(\mathcal I_n\).
+Keeping one generator from each represented orbit therefore produces a set
+\(\mathcal G_n^R\) with
+\[
+ \card{\mathcal G_n^R}\ge\tfrac12A_n^R(v,\delta),
+ \qquad L(g)\le n\quad(g\in\mathcal G_n^R),
+\]
+and \(n^{-1}\log R(g)\in(v-\delta,v+\delta)\).
+
+Fix \(0<\alpha<\alpha_+\), set \(\rho=\alpha/v<1\), and put
+\(n_m=\lfloor\rho m\rfloor\).  For \(g\in\mathcal G_{n_m}^R\), define
+\[
+ z_m(g)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  [a]g,&m-L(g)=2a,\\
+  [a]\tau g,&m-L(g)=2a+1.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+The orbit formulas give \(L(z_m(g))=m\) and
+\(R(z_m(g))=R(g)\), so \(z_m(g)\in\mathcal I_m\).  Freeness makes this map
+injective.  From \eqref{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}, first letting
+\(\delta\downarrow0\), we obtain the local counting lower bound
+\begin{equation}
+ \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac1m
+ \log A_m^R(\alpha,\varepsilon)
+ \ge\frac{\alpha}{v}\bigl(P(t)-tv\bigr).
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-orbit-filling}
+\end{equation}
+
+If \(0<\alpha\le v_c\), let \(t\downarrow t_c\) in
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-orbit-filling}; then \(v\downarrow v_c\) and the
+right side tends to \(\sigma_0\alpha\).  If
+\(v_c<\alpha<\alpha_+\), let \(t_\alpha\) be the unique point with
+\(P'(t_\alpha)=\alpha\), and let \(t\downarrow t_\alpha\) through values with
+\(P'(t)>\alpha\).  The right side then tends to
+\(P(t_\alpha)-t_\alpha\alpha\).  In both cases this is
+\(\log\varphi-I(\alpha)\).  Division by
+\(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\) proves the LDP lower bound at every interior
+point of the effective domain.
+
+The effective domain and the affine formula follow from the same convex-dual
+calculation as in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp}, since the pressure is the same.
+At \(0\), the left endpoint \(F_{m+1}-1\) has \(R=1\) and supplies the lower
+bound directly.  At \(\alpha_+\), use interior points tending to the endpoint
+and continuity of the finite convex rate on \([0,\alpha_+]\).  Hence the
+lower bound holds for every open set, completing the full LDP.
+\end{proof}

 Date of search: 2026-08-02 (Asia/Singapore).
 
+## Named-problem and standard-object audit (2026-08-14)
+
+The search was repeated against primary texts and four bibliographic
+services.  The arXiv Atom query 'all:"Fibonacci partition"' returned twelve
+records.  Crossref DOI records and zbMATH Open confirmed the publication
+metadata below.  Semantic Scholar's DOI endpoint returned Weinstein's
+six-item citation graph and the five-item citation graph of Chow--Slattery;
+its free-text endpoint and a later request for the 2022 paper returned HTTP
+429.  Exact-phrase arXiv and Crossref searches, the available citation
+graphs, and full-text checks of the later Fibonacci-partition papers located
+no resolution of the following three problems.  This is evidence of current
+status, not a claim of exhaustive priority.
+
+1. F. V. Weinstein, *Notes on Fibonacci Partitions*, Experimental
+   Mathematics 25 (2016), 482--499,
+   doi:10.1080/10586458.2015.1118416, p. 18:
+   **"How to describe the set of F-primitive numbers?"**
+
+   The paper's weighted-generator renewal
+   (prop:weighted-generator-renewal) and Tauberian law
+   (thm:psi-tauberian) enumerate Weinstein generators by multiplier and
+   cost.  They do not decide whether the *minimal integer* at a fixed
+   multiplier is f-simple.  The missing step is an order-sensitive
+   comparison excluding every non-simple orbit representative below the
+   least simple representative.
+
+2. Weinstein, ibid., Conjecture 9.1, pp. 19--20:
+   **"Then \(C_i\) coincides with the convex hull of the set of points
+   \((c,F(c))\)"** for the explicitly defined sets \(B_1(i)\), and also
+   \(B_2(i)\) in even layers.
+
+   The interval identity (thm:fiber-partition-interval) canonically
+   recovers every value of the standard function \(R=F\) on these layers,
+   and thm:unconditional-extremal-fibers proves the top horizontal support
+   value and all its maximizers.  The conjecture requires every supporting
+   slope.  What is missing is a uniform supporting-line inequality for all
+   partition values, not another maximum computation.
+
+3. F. V. Weinstein, *On a theorem of J. Shallit concerning Fibonacci
+   partitions*, Communications in Mathematics 30 (2022), 203--207,
+   doi:10.46298/cm.10769, Conjecture 3.3, p. 207:
+   **"\(r_3^{(a,i,b)}(n)-r_3^{(a,j,b)}(n)\le1\) for any
+   \(i,j\in\{0,1,2\}\). Moreover, [the product of the three pairwise
+   differences] \(=0\)."**
+
+   The coefficient-spectrum identity in thm:affine-transfer starts from
+   the same truncated product, and a part-count mark replaces it by
+   \(\prod_{r=a}^b(1+u z^{f_r})\).  The present Fourier formulas act on the
+   value coordinate only.  The missing input is a roots-of-unity
+   cancellation theorem at \(u^3=1\), uniform in \(a,b,n\); no such estimate
+   follows from the unmarked renewal.
+
+### Closed false lead
+
+Chow--Slattery, *On Fibonacci partitions*, J. Number Theory 225 (2021),
+310--326, Conjecture 1.4, asked whether
+**"\(B(H)\to B\) \((H\to\infty)\)"**.  This is not still open.  Zhou,
+*On the Representation Functions of Certain Numeration Systems*,
+arXiv:2305.00792, Corollary 1.5, explicitly states that its Fibonacci
+specialization solves Conjecture 1.4 and the first three problems on
+Chow--Slattery p. 315.  It is therefore excluded from the candidate list.
+
+### A/B/C/D decision
+
+- **(A):** The three live problems are genuine, but the manuscript lacks the
+  order-sensitive minimum comparison, all-slope support inequalities, and
+  roots-of-unity cancellation they respectively require.
+- **(B):** The exact identity
+  \(d_m(x)=R(\chi_m(x))\) maps the bespoke fibers bijectively to two standard
+  Fibonacci layers.  More strongly, the already proved generator renewal has
+  exact one-layer weights \(2,1\).  This route is selected.
+- **(C):** The main pressure and LDP are already unconditional.  The local
+  prime-support theorem stops at an active-cutoff stable/semistable renewal
+  input; the dyadic infinite-variance and no-positive-exponential-moment
+  calculation shows that this is a real obstruction, not a removable
+  Gaussian hypothesis.
+- **(D):** The largest-fiber formulas, freezing boundary, critical constants,
+  and LDP exponent are already sharp.  The compact-operator obstruction has
+  no plausible converse without specifying an operator class beyond the
+  hypotheses it rules out.
+
+The selected theorem is now thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics: all-real
+pressure, frozen unnormalized limit, critical \(2m/\mu_C\) law, critical
+Gibbs coexistence, and a full LDP for \(m^{-1}\log R(n)\) under the uniform
+law on one standard Fibonacci layer.  Its LDP lower bound uses one-layer
+orbit weights directly; it is not inferred from a two-layer mixture.
+

+def critical_single_layer_partition(layer: int, renewal: list[float]) -> float:
+    """Evaluate the exact one-layer critical partition function from u_j."""
+    if layer < 1 or layer >= len(renewal):
+        raise ValueError("renewal coefficients must be available through layer")
+    return 2.0 * sum(renewal[:layer]) + renewal[layer] - 1.0
+
+
+def single_layer_orbit_counter(
+    layer: int, generators: list[Counter[int]]
+) -> Counter[int]:
+    """Recover the standard Fibonacci-partition spectrum on one layer."""
+    if layer < 1 or layer >= len(generators):
+        raise ValueError("generator table must include costs through layer")
+    levels: Counter[int] = Counter({1: 1})
+    for cost in range(1, layer + 1):
+        orbit_weight = 2 if cost < layer else 1
+        for level, word_count in generators[cost].items():
+            levels[level] += orbit_weight * word_count
+    return levels
+

-\begin{abstract}

-\(D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\) for \(m\ge6\), together with all maximizing
- residues.  For real negative tilts we
-prove a Dirichlet-series freezing bound.  If \(\sigma_0>2\) is determined by

-\(\lim_{m\to\infty}m^{-1}\log\sum_x d_m(x)^t=0\) for every

-Weinstein's orbit formulas, including the exceptional levels and early
-layers.  At the finer, unnormalized scale, the fixed multiplicity counts

-\(4(2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s))^{-1}-2\) for \(s>\sigma_0\), with a simple pole
-at \(\sigma_0\) and a total-variation Gibbs limit.  A Wiener--Ikehara

+\begin{abstract}
+Let \(R(n)\) be the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct Fibonacci
+numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  On the standard Fibonacci layer
+\(\mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1)\), we determine the all-real moment
+pressure of \(R\).  If \(\sigma_0>2\) is defined by
+\(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\), this pressure is zero for
+\(t\le-\sigma_0\), positive, real analytic, and strictly convex for
+\(t>-\sigma_0\), and has a first-order corner at the endpoint.  At criticality
+the one-layer partition sum is asymptotic to \(2m/\mu_C\), and its Gibbs law
+converges to a uniform mixture of generating-layer fractions.  Under the
+uniform law on \(\mathcal I_m\), \(m^{-1}\log R(n)\) satisfies a full large
+deviation principle; the rate is affine on the coexistence interval.  The
+proof uses a weighted renewal identity for Weinstein's free generators,
+published Stern--Brocot denominator pressure, and a parity-free orbit-filling
+argument for the nonexposed slopes.
+
+A finite-window Zeckendorf fold provides an exact finite model for the same
+spectrum: its fiber list is the list of \(R\) on two consecutive layers.
+An affine permutation also identifies each fiber with a finite Fibonacci
+subset-sum coefficient and a partition-function difference.  This yields the
+exact largest fibers
+\(D_{2k}=F_{k+2}\), \(D_{2k+1}=2F_{k+1}\), and
+\(D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\), including every maximizing residue.  The two-layer
+model has the same pressure and large-deviation rate, an exact frozen
+Dirichlet limit, and a critical finite-size constant \(4/\mu_C\).  The frozen
+half-line also rules out a globally analytic compact-operator representation
+under precise spectral hypotheses.
+\end{abstract}

+\section{Thermodynamics of the Fibonacci partition function}
+\label{sec:standard-thermodynamics}
+
+The renewal identity was derived from Weinstein's standard Fibonacci
+partition function before it was transferred to the finite-window fold.  We
+now state its one-layer consequences intrinsically.  This removes the bespoke
+fold from the probabilistic conclusions.
+
+For \(m\ge1\), recall
+\[
+ \mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1)
+\]
+and define
+\[
+ Z_m^R(t):=\sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^t
+ \qquad(t\in\RR).
+\]
+If \(\mathbf N_m\) is uniform on \(\mathcal I_m\), put
+\[
+ Y_m^R:=\frac1m\log R(\mathbf N_m).
+\]
+
+\begin{theorem}[One-layer Fibonacci partition thermodynamics]
+\label{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics}
+For every \(t\in\RR\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log Z_m^R(t)=P(t),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-pressure}
+\end{equation}
+where \(P\) is the pressure in \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure}.  Thus the
+one-layer pressure is zero on \((-\infty,-\sigma_0]\), is positive, real
+analytic, and strictly convex on \((-\sigma_0,\infty)\), and has the
+one-sided derivatives in \eqref{eq:critical-pressure-slopes}.
+
+For \(s>\sigma_0\), the unnormalized sums satisfy
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-s)\longrightarrow
+ \mathcal Z_R(s):=
+ \frac2{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-1.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-frozen-limit}
+\end{equation}
+At the critical tilt,
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)\sim\frac{2m}{\mu_C}.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}
+\end{equation}
+
+For \(n\in\mathcal I_m\) with \(R(n)>2\), let \(g(n)\) be the generating
+number of its Weinstein orbit and put \(\ell_m^R(n)=L(g(n))\); set
+\(\ell_m^R(n)=0\) when \(R(n)\le2\).  Let \(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m\) have the
+critical Gibbs law
+\[
+ \Pr\{\widehat{\mathbf N}_m=n\}
+ =\frac{R(n)^{-\sigma_0}}{Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)}
+ \qquad(n\in\mathcal I_m).
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}
+ \left(
+  \frac1m\log R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m),
+  \frac1m\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)
+ \right)
+ \xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{\mathrm d}(v_cU,U),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-gibbs}
+\end{equation}
+where \(U\) is uniform on \([0,1]\).
+
+Finally, \((Y_m^R)\) satisfies a full large deviation principle with speed
+\(m\) and the good rate function
+\begin{equation}
+ I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}
+ \{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-ldp-rate}
+\end{equation}
+Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), where
+\(\alpha_+=\tfrac12\log\varphi\), and
+\[
+ I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
+ \qquad(0\le\alpha\le v_c).
+\]
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put \(H_m(s)=\sum_{j=0}^m u_j(s)\).  The exact one-layer renewal identity
+\eqref{eq:weighted-layer-renewal} says
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-s)=2H_{m-1}(s)+u_m(s)-1.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-renewal}
+\end{equation}
+The proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} established
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log u_m(s)
+ =\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log H_m(s)
+ =P(-s).
+\]
+Since \(u_m(s)\le Z_m^R(-s)\le3H_m(s)\), this proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure}.
+
+If \(s>\sigma_0\), then \(U_s(1)=\sum_{j\ge0}u_j(s)<\infty\), so
+\(u_m(s)\to0\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-generating-function} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} give
+\[
+ U_s(1)=\frac1{1-B_s(1)}
+ =\frac1{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}.
+\]
+Letting \(m\to\infty\) in \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-frozen-limit}.  At \(s=\sigma_0\), the arithmetic
+renewal theorem used in \Cref{thm:critical-finite-window-gibbs} gives
+\(u_m(\sigma_0)\to1/\mu_C\).  Ces\`aro summation in
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}.
+
+We next retain the generating cost.  The four orbit branches displayed above
+\eqref{eq:marked-microcanonical-count} show that a generator of cost \(c\)
+contributes two points to \(\mathcal I_m\) if \(c<m\), one if \(c=m\), and
+none if \(c>m\).  Thus the one-layer boundary weight is
+\[
+ K_m^R(c)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  2,&c<m,\\
+  1,&c=m,\\
+  0,&c>m.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+With the marked renewal measure \(\mathcal U\) defined before
+\eqref{eq:marked-microcanonical-count}, the same free-monoid bijection gives,
+for every Borel set
+\(B\subset\mathbb R\times(\log2,\infty)\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \card{\{n\in\mathcal I_m:
+   (\ell_m^R(n),\log R(n))\in B\}}
+ =\int_B K_m^R(c)e^{\sigma_0h}\,\mathcal U(dc,dh).
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-marked-count}
+\end{equation}
+The points with \(R(n)\le2\) have bounded total critical weight, uniformly in
+\(m\), by the uniform layer-count lemma.
+
+For every bounded continuous \(f\) on \([0,1]\), the arithmetic renewal
+theorem and a Riemann-sum argument give
+\[
+ \frac1m\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_j(\sigma_0)f(j/m)
+ \longrightarrow\frac1{\mu_C}\int_0^1f(y)\,dy.
+\]
+After multiplication of \eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} by
+\(e^{-\sigma_0h}\), the weights are two for \(j<m\) and one at \(j=m\).
+Together with \eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}, this proves
+\[
+ \frac{\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)}m
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}U.
+\]
+For the reward coordinate, the critical renewal increments
+\((C_i,H_i)\) satisfy
+\[
+ \frac{H_1+\cdots+H_r}{C_1+\cdots+C_r}
+ \longrightarrow\frac{\mu_H}{\mu_C}=v_c
+\quad\text{almost surely}.
+\]
+Every cost increment is at least three.  Consequently the number of renewal
+epochs with total cost at most \(m\) and reward-to-cost ratio outside a fixed
+\(\delta\)-neighborhood of \(v_c\) is \(o(m)\), pathwise and, by bounded
+convergence after division by \(m\), in expectation.  Since \(K_m^R\le2\),
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} and
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size} imply
+\[
+ \frac1m\log R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)
+ -v_c\frac{\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)}m
+ \xrightarrow{\Pr}0.
+\]
+This proves \eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-gibbs}.
+
+It remains to prove the full LDP, in particular the lower bound at the
+nonexposed slopes.  The layer has
+\(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\), and hence
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log\card{\mathcal I_m}=\log\varphi.
+\]
+Equation \eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure} therefore gives the limiting
+logarithmic moment generating function
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m
+ \log\mathbb E e^{tmY_m^R}=P(t)-\log\varphi.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-log-mgf}
+\]
+The translated extremal theorem in the Fibonacci-convention lemma gives
+\[
+ \max_{n\in\mathcal I_m}\frac1m\log R(n)
+ \longrightarrow\alpha_+.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-maximum}
+\]
+Indeed, the two shifted endpoints have partition value one, so they do not
+change the maximum on the intervening Fibonacci block.  Thus the variables
+are exponentially tight, and the G\"artner--Ellis upper bound gives the
+required upper bound for closed sets.
+
+For the lower bound, fix \(t>t_c=-\sigma_0\), write \(v=P'(t)>v_c\), and
+tilt the uniform law on \(\mathcal I_n\) by \(R(k)^t\).  Analyticity of \(P\)
+and the exponential Markov inequality applied to
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure} show that this tilted law assigns
+exponentially vanishing mass to
+\[
+ \left\{k\in\mathcal I_n:
+   \left|n^{-1}\log R(k)-v\right|\ge\delta\right\}.
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ A_n^R(v,\delta)
+ :=\card{\{k\in\mathcal I_n:
+ |n^{-1}\log R(k)-v|<\delta\}},
+\]
+then
+\begin{equation}
+ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log A_n^R(v,\delta)
+ \ge P(t)-tv-|t|\delta.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}
+\end{equation}
+
+For large \(n\), every point counted here has multiplicity greater than two.
+Each generating orbit contributes at most two points to \(\mathcal I_n\).
+Keeping one generator from each represented orbit therefore produces a set
+\(\mathcal G_n^R\) with
+\[
+ \card{\mathcal G_n^R}\ge\tfrac12A_n^R(v,\delta),
+ \qquad L(g)\le n\quad(g\in\mathcal G_n^R),
+\]
+and \(n^{-1}\log R(g)\in(v-\delta,v+\delta)\).
+
+Fix \(0<\alpha<\alpha_+\), set \(\rho=\alpha/v<1\), and put
+\(n_m=\lfloor\rho m\rfloor\).  For \(g\in\mathcal G_{n_m}^R\), define
+\[
+ z_m(g)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  [a]g,&m-L(g)=2a,\\
+  [a]\tau g,&m-L(g)=2a+1.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+The orbit formulas give \(L(z_m(g))=m\) and
+\(R(z_m(g))=R(g)\), so \(z_m(g)\in\mathcal I_m\).  Freeness makes this map
+injective.  From \eqref{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}, first letting
+\(\delta\downarrow0\), we obtain the local counting lower bound
+\begin{equation}
+ \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac1m
+ \log A_m^R(\alpha,\varepsilon)
+ \ge\frac{\alpha}{v}\bigl(P(t)-tv\bigr).
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-orbit-filling}
+\end{equation}
+
+If \(0<\alpha\le v_c\), let \(t\downarrow t_c\) in
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-orbit-filling}; then \(v\downarrow v_c\) and the
+right side tends to \(\sigma_0\alpha\).  If
+\(v_c<\alpha<\alpha_+\), let \(t_\alpha\) be the unique point with
+\(P'(t_\alpha)=\alpha\), and let \(t\downarrow t_\alpha\) through values with
+\(P'(t)>\alpha\).  The right side then tends to
+\(P(t_\alpha)-t_\alpha\alpha\).  In both cases this is
+\(\log\varphi-I(\alpha)\).  Division by
+\(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\) proves the LDP lower bound at every interior
+point of the effective domain.
+
+The effective domain and the affine formula follow from the same convex-dual
+calculation as in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp}, since the pressure is the same.
+At \(0\), the left endpoint \(F_{m+1}-1\) has \(R=1\) and supplies the lower
+bound directly.  At \(\alpha_+\), use interior points tending to the endpoint
+and continuity of the finite convex rate on \([0,\alpha_+]\).  Hence the
+lower bound holds for every open set, completing the full LDP.
+\end{proof}

The Editors
Transactions of the American Mathematical Society

Dear Editors,

We submit for your consideration the manuscript "Fibonacci Partition
Thermodynamics and Finite-Window Zeckendorf Fibers."

The paper studies the fibers of a finite-window map that reduces a binary
Fibonacci sum modulo the next Fibonacci number and selects the corresponding
legal visible word. Its principal result is an explicit affine permutation
identifying individual fiber multiplicities with coefficients of a finite
Fibonacci subset-sum polynomial and with Fibonacci-lag differences of the
classical partition function. A complementary interval identity identifies
the complete fiber list with ordinary partition values on two consecutive
Fibonacci layers. After a precise translation of Fibonacci conventions, this
transfers the known extremal classification and gives all largest fibers and
maximizing residues.

The second principal result is a negative-temperature freezing theorem. Using
Weinstein's orbit counts, with the low levels, endpoints, and early layers
treated explicitly, the paper proves that the real-tilt pressure vanishes for
all t at or below the exact threshold determined by
zeta(sigma_0-1)/zeta(sigma_0)=2. A precise analytic-perturbation argument then
rules out a globally analytic compact-operator representation under stated
spectral hypotheses. The full real-tilt large deviation principle is stated
only as a conditional corollary; its residual pressure hypothesis remains
open.

Supporting results transfer Sanna's integer partition power-sum constants to
the finite-window moments, give a direct cubic recurrence for the quadratic
moment, and isolate a diagonal high-tilt consequence. Sanna's previously
published endpoint law is explicitly credited as prior work.

The manuscript does not assert a finite-state normalization transducer,
collision kernel, recurrence-polynomial certificate, Galois-group result, or
Chebotarev theorem. Those claims and their computational artifacts have been
withdrawn.

The manuscript is 30 pages in amsart format and is self-contained apart from
the cited results that are transferred with explicit convention dictionaries.

Thank you for considering this submission.

Sincerely,
The Authors

+## Named-problem and standard-object audit (2026-08-14)
+
+The search was repeated against primary texts and four bibliographic
+services.  The arXiv Atom query 'all:"Fibonacci partition"' returned twelve
+records.  Crossref DOI records and zbMATH Open confirmed the publication
+metadata below.  Semantic Scholar's DOI endpoint returned Weinstein's
+six-item citation graph and the five-item citation graph of Chow--Slattery;
+its free-text endpoint and a later request for the 2022 paper returned HTTP
+429.  Exact-phrase arXiv and Crossref searches, the available citation
+graphs, and full-text checks of the later Fibonacci-partition papers located
+no resolution of the following three problems.  This is evidence of current
+status, not a claim of exhaustive priority.
+
+1. F. V. Weinstein, *Notes on Fibonacci Partitions*, Experimental
+   Mathematics 25 (2016), 482--499,
+   doi:10.1080/10586458.2015.1118416, p. 18:
+   **"How to describe the set of F-primitive numbers?"**
+
+   The paper's weighted-generator renewal
+   (prop:weighted-generator-renewal) and Tauberian law
+   (thm:psi-tauberian) enumerate Weinstein generators by multiplier and
+   cost.  They do not decide whether the *minimal integer* at a fixed
+   multiplier is f-simple.  The missing step is an order-sensitive
+   comparison excluding every non-simple orbit representative below the
+   least simple representative.
+
+2. Weinstein, ibid., Conjecture 9.1, pp. 19--20:
+   **"Then \(C_i\) coincides with the convex hull of the set of points
+   \((c,F(c))\)"** for the explicitly defined sets \(B_1(i)\), and also
+   \(B_2(i)\) in even layers.
+
+   The interval identity (thm:fiber-partition-interval) canonically
+   recovers every value of the standard function \(R=F\) on these layers,
+   and thm:unconditional-extremal-fibers proves the top horizontal support
+   value and all its maximizers.  The conjecture requires every supporting
+   slope.  What is missing is a uniform supporting-line inequality for all
+   partition values, not another maximum computation.
+
+3. F. V. Weinstein, *On a theorem of J. Shallit concerning Fibonacci
+   partitions*, Communications in Mathematics 30 (2022), 203--207,
+   doi:10.46298/cm.10769, Conjecture 3.3, p. 207:
+   **"\(r_3^{(a,i,b)}(n)-r_3^{(a,j,b)}(n)\le1\) for any
+   \(i,j\in\{0,1,2\}\). Moreover, [the product of the three pairwise
+   differences] \(=0\)."**
+
+   The coefficient-spectrum identity in thm:affine-transfer starts from
+   the same truncated product, and a part-count mark replaces it by
+   \(\prod_{r=a}^b(1+u z^{f_r})\).  The present Fourier formulas act on the
+   value coordinate only.  The missing input is a roots-of-unity
+   cancellation theorem at \(u^3=1\), uniform in \(a,b,n\); no such estimate
+   follows from the unmarked renewal.
+
+### Closed false lead
+
+Chow--Slattery, *On Fibonacci partitions*, J. Number Theory 225 (2021),
+310--326, Conjecture 1.4, asked whether
+**"\(B(H)\to B\) \((H\to\infty)\)"**.  This is not still open.  Zhou,
+*On the Representation Functions of Certain Numeration Systems*,
+arXiv:2305.00792, Corollary 1.5, explicitly states that its Fibonacci
+specialization solves Conjecture 1.4 and the first three problems on
+Chow--Slattery p. 315.  It is therefore excluded from the candidate list.
+
+### A/B/C/D decision
+
+- **(A):** The three live problems are genuine, but the manuscript lacks the
+  order-sensitive minimum comparison, all-slope support inequalities, and
+  roots-of-unity cancellation they respectively require.
+- **(B):** The exact identity
+  \(d_m(x)=R(\chi_m(x))\) maps the bespoke fibers bijectively to two standard
+  Fibonacci layers.  More strongly, the already proved generator renewal has
+  exact one-layer weights \(2,1\).  This route is selected.
+- **(C):** The main pressure and LDP are already unconditional.  The local
+  prime-support theorem stops at an active-cutoff stable/semistable renewal
+  input; the dyadic infinite-variance and no-positive-exponential-moment
+  calculation shows that this is a real obstruction, not a removable
+  Gaussian hypothesis.
+- **(D):** The largest-fiber formulas, freezing boundary, critical constants,
+  and LDP exponent are already sharp.  The compact-operator obstruction has
+  no plausible converse without specifying an operator class beyond the
+  hypotheses it rules out.
+
+The selected theorem is now thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics: all-real
+pressure, frozen unnormalized limit, critical \(2m/\mu_C\) law, critical
+Gibbs coexistence, and a full LDP for \(m^{-1}\log R(n)\) under the uniform
+law on one standard Fibonacci layer.  Its LDP lower bound uses one-layer
+orbit weights directly; it is not inferred from a two-layer mixture.
+

+def critical_single_layer_partition(layer: int, renewal: list[float]) -> float:
+    """Evaluate the exact one-layer critical partition function from u_j."""
+    if layer < 1 or layer >= len(renewal):
+        raise ValueError("renewal coefficients must be available through layer")
+    return 2.0 * sum(renewal[:layer]) + renewal[layer] - 1.0
+
+
+def single_layer_orbit_counter(
+    layer: int, generators: list[Counter[int]]
+) -> Counter[int]:
+    """Recover the standard Fibonacci-partition spectrum on one layer."""
+    if layer < 1 or layer >= len(generators):
+        raise ValueError("generator table must include costs through layer")
+    levels: Counter[int] = Counter({1: 1})
+    for cost in range(1, layer + 1):
+        orbit_weight = 2 if cost < layer else 1
+        for level, word_count in generators[cost].items():
+            levels[level] += orbit_weight * word_count
+    return levels
+

-We study the fibers of a finite-window map that sends a binary Fibonacci sum
-to the legal word representing its residue modulo the next Fibonacci number.
-An explicit affine permutation identifies the fiber multiplicities with the
-coefficients of a finite Fibonacci subset-sum polynomial and, pointwise, with
-a Fibonacci-lag difference of the classical partition function.  A second

-these intervals then gives
-\(D_{2k}=F_{k+2}\), \(D_{2k+1}=2F_{k+1}\), and
-\(D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\) for \(m\ge6\), together with all maximizing
- residues.  For real negative tilts we
-prove a Dirichlet-series freezing bound.  If \(\sigma_0>2\) is determined by

-\(\lim_{m\to\infty}m^{-1}\log\sum_x d_m(x)^t=0\) for every
-\(t\le-\sigma_0\).  The endpoint proof uses an explicit transfer of
-Weinstein's orbit formulas, including the exceptional levels and early
-layers.  At the finer, unnormalized scale, the fixed multiplicity counts
-stabilize and the negative-tilt sums converge exactly to
-\(4(2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s))^{-1}-2\) for \(s>\sigma_0\), with a simple pole
-at \(\sigma_0\) and a total-variation Gibbs limit.  A Wiener--Ikehara
-argument gives the associated generating-orbit asymptotic.  A weighted renewal
-identity for Weinstein's free generators, combined with the published
-Stern--Brocot denominator pressure, proves that the pressure exists for every
-real tilt.  It is real analytic and strictly convex on
-\((-\sigma_0,\infty)\), but has a first-order corner at \(-\sigma_0\).
-Exactly at that corner the unnormalized partition function grows linearly,
-and the critical finite-window Gibbs law converges to a uniform mixture of
-coexisting layer fractions; its log multiplicity is locked to the layer
-fraction by the critical velocity.

+Let \(R(n)\) be the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct Fibonacci
+numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  On the standard Fibonacci layer
+\(\mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1)\), we determine the all-real moment
+pressure of \(R\).  If \(\sigma_0>2\) is defined by
+\(\zeta(\sigma_0-1)/\zeta(\sigma_0)=2\), this pressure is zero for
+\(t\le-\sigma_0\), positive, real analytic, and strictly convex for
+\(t>-\sigma_0\), and has a first-order corner at the endpoint.  At criticality
+the one-layer partition sum is asymptotic to \(2m/\mu_C\), and its Gibbs law
+converges to a uniform mixture of generating-layer fractions.  Under the

+deviation principle; the rate is affine on the coexistence interval.  The
+proof uses a weighted renewal identity for Weinstein's free generators,
+published Stern--Brocot denominator pressure, and a parity-free orbit-filling
+argument for the nonexposed slopes.
+

+spectrum: its fiber list is the list of \(R\) on two consecutive layers.
+An affine permutation also identifies each fiber with a finite Fibonacci
+subset-sum coefficient and a partition-function difference.  This yields the
+exact largest fibers
+\(D_{2k}=F_{k+2}\), \(D_{2k+1}=2F_{k+1}\), and
+\(D_m=D_{m-2}+D_{m-4}\), including every maximizing residue.  The two-layer
+model has the same pressure and large-deviation rate, an exact frozen
+Dirichlet limit, and a critical finite-size constant \(4/\mu_C\).  The frozen
+half-line also rules out a globally analytic compact-operator representation
+under precise spectral hypotheses.
+\end{abstract}

+\section{Thermodynamics of the Fibonacci partition function}
+\label{sec:standard-thermodynamics}
+
+The renewal identity was derived from Weinstein's standard Fibonacci
+partition function before it was transferred to the finite-window fold.  We
+now state its one-layer consequences intrinsically.  This removes the bespoke
+fold from the probabilistic conclusions.
+
+For \(m\ge1\), recall
+\[
+ \mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1)
+\]
+and define
+\[
+ Z_m^R(t):=\sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^t
+ \qquad(t\in\RR).
+\]
+If \(\mathbf N_m\) is uniform on \(\mathcal I_m\), put
+\[
+ Y_m^R:=\frac1m\log R(\mathbf N_m).
+\]
+
+\begin{theorem}[One-layer Fibonacci partition thermodynamics]
+\label{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics}
+For every \(t\in\RR\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log Z_m^R(t)=P(t),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-pressure}
+\end{equation}
+where \(P\) is the pressure in \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure}.  Thus the
+one-layer pressure is zero on \((-\infty,-\sigma_0]\), is positive, real
+analytic, and strictly convex on \((-\sigma_0,\infty)\), and has the
+one-sided derivatives in \eqref{eq:critical-pressure-slopes}.
+
+For \(s>\sigma_0\), the unnormalized sums satisfy
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-s)\longrightarrow
+ \mathcal Z_R(s):=
+ \frac2{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-1.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-frozen-limit}
+\end{equation}
+At the critical tilt,
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)\sim\frac{2m}{\mu_C}.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}
+\end{equation}
+
+For \(n\in\mathcal I_m\) with \(R(n)>2\), let \(g(n)\) be the generating
+number of its Weinstein orbit and put \(\ell_m^R(n)=L(g(n))\); set
+\(\ell_m^R(n)=0\) when \(R(n)\le2\).  Let \(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m\) have the
+critical Gibbs law
+\[
+ \Pr\{\widehat{\mathbf N}_m=n\}
+ =\frac{R(n)^{-\sigma_0}}{Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)}
+ \qquad(n\in\mathcal I_m).
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}
+ \left(
+  \frac1m\log R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m),
+  \frac1m\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)
+ \right)
+ \xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{\mathrm d}(v_cU,U),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-gibbs}
+\end{equation}
+where \(U\) is uniform on \([0,1]\).
+
+Finally, \((Y_m^R)\) satisfies a full large deviation principle with speed
+\(m\) and the good rate function
+\begin{equation}
+ I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}
+ \{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-ldp-rate}
+\end{equation}
+Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), where
+\(\alpha_+=\tfrac12\log\varphi\), and
+\[
+ I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
+ \qquad(0\le\alpha\le v_c).
+\]
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put \(H_m(s)=\sum_{j=0}^m u_j(s)\).  The exact one-layer renewal identity
+\eqref{eq:weighted-layer-renewal} says
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-s)=2H_{m-1}(s)+u_m(s)-1.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-renewal}
+\end{equation}
+The proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} established
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log u_m(s)
+ =\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log H_m(s)
+ =P(-s).
+\]
+Since \(u_m(s)\le Z_m^R(-s)\le3H_m(s)\), this proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure}.
+
+If \(s>\sigma_0\), then \(U_s(1)=\sum_{j\ge0}u_j(s)<\infty\), so
+\(u_m(s)\to0\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-generating-function} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} give
+\[
+ U_s(1)=\frac1{1-B_s(1)}
+ =\frac1{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}.
+\]
+Letting \(m\to\infty\) in \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-frozen-limit}.  At \(s=\sigma_0\), the arithmetic
+renewal theorem used in \Cref{thm:critical-finite-window-gibbs} gives
+\(u_m(\sigma_0)\to1/\mu_C\).  Ces\`aro summation in
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}.
+
+We next retain the generating cost.  The four orbit branches displayed above
+\eqref{eq:marked-microcanonical-count} show that a generator of cost \(c\)
+contributes two points to \(\mathcal I_m\) if \(c<m\), one if \(c=m\), and
+none if \(c>m\).  Thus the one-layer boundary weight is
+\[
+ K_m^R(c)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  2,&c<m,\\
+  1,&c=m,\\
+  0,&c>m.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+With the marked renewal measure \(\mathcal U\) defined before
+\eqref{eq:marked-microcanonical-count}, the same free-monoid bijection gives,
+for every Borel set
+\(B\subset\mathbb R\times(\log2,\infty)\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \card{\{n\in\mathcal I_m:
+   (\ell_m^R(n),\log R(n))\in B\}}
+ =\int_B K_m^R(c)e^{\sigma_0h}\,\mathcal U(dc,dh).
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-marked-count}
+\end{equation}
+The points with \(R(n)\le2\) have bounded total critical weight, uniformly in
+\(m\), by the uniform layer-count lemma.
+
+For every bounded continuous \(f\) on \([0,1]\), the arithmetic renewal
+theorem and a Riemann-sum argument give
+\[
+ \frac1m\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_j(\sigma_0)f(j/m)
+ \longrightarrow\frac1{\mu_C}\int_0^1f(y)\,dy.
+\]
+After multiplication of \eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} by
+\(e^{-\sigma_0h}\), the weights are two for \(j<m\) and one at \(j=m\).
+Together with \eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}, this proves
+\[
+ \frac{\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)}m
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}U.
+\]
+For the reward coordinate, the critical renewal increments
+\((C_i,H_i)\) satisfy
+\[
+ \frac{H_1+\cdots+H_r}{C_1+\cdots+C_r}
+ \longrightarrow\frac{\mu_H}{\mu_C}=v_c
+\quad\text{almost surely}.
+\]
+Every cost increment is at least three.  Consequently the number of renewal
+epochs with total cost at most \(m\) and reward-to-cost ratio outside a fixed
+\(\delta\)-neighborhood of \(v_c\) is \(o(m)\), pathwise and, by bounded
+convergence after division by \(m\), in expectation.  Since \(K_m^R\le2\),
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} and
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size} imply
+\[
+ \frac1m\log R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)
+ -v_c\frac{\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)}m
+ \xrightarrow{\Pr}0.
+\]
+This proves \eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-gibbs}.
+
+It remains to prove the full LDP, in particular the lower bound at the
+nonexposed slopes.  The layer has
+\(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\), and hence
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log\card{\mathcal I_m}=\log\varphi.
+\]
+Equation \eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure} therefore gives the limiting
+logarithmic moment generating function
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m
+ \log\mathbb E e^{tmY_m^R}=P(t)-\log\varphi.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-log-mgf}
+\]
+The translated extremal theorem in the Fibonacci-convention lemma gives
+\[
+ \max_{n\in\mathcal I_m}\frac1m\log R(n)
+ \longrightarrow\alpha_+.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-maximum}
+\]
+Indeed, the two shifted endpoints have partition value one, so they do not
+change the maximum on the intervening Fibonacci block.  Thus the variables
+are exponentially tight, and the G\"artner--Ellis upper bound gives the
+required upper bound for closed sets.
+
+For the lower bound, fix \(t>t_c=-\sigma_0\), write \(v=P'(t)>v_c\), and
+tilt the uniform law on \(\mathcal I_n\) by \(R(k)^t\).  Analyticity of \(P\)
+and the exponential Markov inequality applied to
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure} show that this tilted law assigns
+exponentially vanishing mass to
+\[
+ \left\{k\in\mathcal I_n:
+   \left|n^{-1}\log R(k)-v\right|\ge\delta\right\}.
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ A_n^R(v,\delta)
+ :=\card{\{k\in\mathcal I_n:
+ |n^{-1}\log R(k)-v|<\delta\}},
+\]
+then
+\begin{equation}
+ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log A_n^R(v,\delta)
+ \ge P(t)-tv-|t|\delta.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}
+\end{equation}
+
+For large \(n\), every point counted here has multiplicity greater than two.
+Each generating orbit contributes at most two points to \(\mathcal I_n\).
+Keeping one generator from each represented orbit therefore produces a set
+\(\mathcal G_n^R\) with
+\[
+ \card{\mathcal G_n^R}\ge\tfrac12A_n^R(v,\delta),
+ \qquad L(g)\le n\quad(g\in\mathcal G_n^R),
+\]
+and \(n^{-1}\log R(g)\in(v-\delta,v+\delta)\).
+
+Fix \(0<\alpha<\alpha_+\), set \(\rho=\alpha/v<1\), and put
+\(n_m=\lfloor\rho m\rfloor\).  For \(g\in\mathcal G_{n_m}^R\), define
+\[
+ z_m(g)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  [a]g,&m-L(g)=2a,\\
+  [a]\tau g,&m-L(g)=2a+1.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+The orbit formulas give \(L(z_m(g))=m\) and
+\(R(z_m(g))=R(g)\), so \(z_m(g)\in\mathcal I_m\).  Freeness makes this map
+injective.  From \eqref{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}, first letting
+\(\delta\downarrow0\), we obtain the local counting lower bound
+\begin{equation}
+ \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac1m
+ \log A_m^R(\alpha,\varepsilon)
+ \ge\frac{\alpha}{v}\bigl(P(t)-tv\bigr).
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-orbit-filling}
+\end{equation}
+
+If \(0<\alpha\le v_c\), let \(t\downarrow t_c\) in
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-orbit-filling}; then \(v\downarrow v_c\) and the
+right side tends to \(\sigma_0\alpha\).  If
+\(v_c<\alpha<\alpha_+\), let \(t_\alpha\) be the unique point with
+\(P'(t_\alpha)=\alpha\), and let \(t\downarrow t_\alpha\) through values with
+\(P'(t)>\alpha\).  The right side then tends to
+\(P(t_\alpha)-t_\alpha\alpha\).  In both cases this is
+\(\log\varphi-I(\alpha)\).  Division by
+\(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\) proves the LDP lower bound at every interior
+point of the effective domain.
+
+The effective domain and the affine formula follow from the same convex-dual
+calculation as in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp}, since the pressure is the same.
+At \(0\), the left endpoint \(F_{m+1}-1\) has \(R=1\) and supplies the lower
+bound directly.  At \(\alpha_+\), use interior points tending to the endpoint
+and continuity of the finite convex rate on \([0,\alpha_+]\).  Hence the
+lower bound holds for every open set, completing the full LDP.
+\end{proof}

 Date of search: 2026-08-02 (Asia/Singapore).
 
+## Named-problem and standard-object audit (2026-08-14)
+
+The search was repeated against primary texts and four bibliographic
+services.  The arXiv Atom query 'all:"Fibonacci partition"' returned twelve
+records.  Crossref DOI records and zbMATH Open confirmed the publication
+metadata below.  Semantic Scholar's DOI endpoint returned Weinstein's
+six-item citation graph and the five-item citation graph of Chow--Slattery;
+its free-text endpoint and a later request for the 2022 paper returned HTTP
+429.  Exact-phrase arXiv and Crossref searches, the available citation
+graphs, and full-text checks of the later Fibonacci-partition papers located
+no resolution of the following three problems.  This is evidence of current
+status, not a claim of exhaustive priority.
+
+1. F. V. Weinstein, *Notes on Fibonacci Partitions*, Experimental
+   Mathematics 25 (2016), 482--499,
+   doi:10.1080/10586458.2015.1118416, p. 18:
+   **"How to describe the set of F-primitive numbers?"**
+
+   The paper's weighted-generator renewal
+   (prop:weighted-generator-renewal) and Tauberian law
+   (thm:psi-tauberian) enumerate Weinstein generators by multiplier and
+   cost.  They do not decide whether the *minimal integer* at a fixed
+   multiplier is f-simple.  The missing step is an order-sensitive
+   comparison excluding every non-simple orbit representative below the
+   least simple representative.
+
+2. Weinstein, ibid., Conjecture 9.1, pp. 19--20:
+   **"Then \(C_i\) coincides with the convex hull of the set of points
+   \((c,F(c))\)"** for the explicitly defined sets \(B_1(i)\), and also
+   \(B_2(i)\) in even layers.
+
+   The interval identity (thm:fiber-partition-interval) canonically
+   recovers every value of the standard function \(R=F\) on these layers,
+   and thm:unconditional-extremal-fibers proves the top horizontal support
+   value and all its maximizers.  The conjecture requires every supporting
+   slope.  What is missing is a uniform supporting-line inequality for all
+   partition values, not another maximum computation.
+
+3. F. V. Weinstein, *On a theorem of J. Shallit concerning Fibonacci
+   partitions*, Communications in Mathematics 30 (2022), 203--207,
+   doi:10.46298/cm.10769, Conjecture 3.3, p. 207:
+   **"\(r_3^{(a,i,b)}(n)-r_3^{(a,j,b)}(n)\le1\) for any
+   \(i,j\in\{0,1,2\}\). Moreover, [the product of the three pairwise
+   differences] \(=0\)."**
+
+   The coefficient-spectrum identity in thm:affine-transfer starts from
+   the same truncated product, and a part-count mark replaces it by
+   \(\prod_{r=a}^b(1+u z^{f_r})\).  The present Fourier formulas act on the
+   value coordinate only.  The missing input is a roots-of-unity
+   cancellation theorem at \(u^3=1\), uniform in \(a,b,n\); no such estimate
+   follows from the unmarked renewal.
+
+### Closed false lead
+
+Chow--Slattery, *On Fibonacci partitions*, J. Number Theory 225 (2021),
+310--326, Conjecture 1.4, asked whether
+**"\(B(H)\to B\) \((H\to\infty)\)"**.  This is not still open.  Zhou,
+*On the Representation Functions of Certain Numeration Systems*,
+arXiv:2305.00792, Corollary 1.5, explicitly states that its Fibonacci
+specialization solves Conjecture 1.4 and the first three problems on
+Chow--Slattery p. 315.  It is therefore excluded from the candidate list.
+
+### A/B/C/D decision
+
+- **(A):** The three live problems are genuine, but the manuscript lacks the
+  order-sensitive minimum comparison, all-slope support inequalities, and
+  roots-of-unity cancellation they respectively require.
+- **(B):** The exact identity
+  \(d_m(x)=R(\chi_m(x))\) maps the bespoke fibers bijectively to two standard
+  Fibonacci layers.  More strongly, the already proved generator renewal has
+  exact one-layer weights \(2,1\).  This route is selected.
+- **(C):** The main pressure and LDP are already unconditional.  The local
+  prime-support theorem stops at an active-cutoff stable/semistable renewal
+  input; the dyadic infinite-variance and no-positive-exponential-moment
+  calculation shows that this is a real obstruction, not a removable
+  Gaussian hypothesis.
+- **(D):** The largest-fiber formulas, freezing boundary, critical constants,
+  and LDP exponent are already sharp.  The compact-operator obstruction has
+  no plausible converse without specifying an operator class beyond the
+  hypotheses it rules out.
+
+The selected theorem is now thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics: all-real
+pressure, frozen unnormalized limit, critical \(2m/\mu_C\) law, critical
+Gibbs coexistence, and a full LDP for \(m^{-1}\log R(n)\) under the uniform
+law on one standard Fibonacci layer.  Its LDP lower bound uses one-layer
+orbit weights directly; it is not inferred from a two-layer mixture.
+

+def critical_single_layer_partition(layer: int, renewal: list[float]) -> float:
+    """Evaluate the exact one-layer critical partition function from u_j."""
+    if layer < 1 or layer >= len(renewal):
+        raise ValueError("renewal coefficients must be available through layer")
+    return 2.0 * sum(renewal[:layer]) + renewal[layer] - 1.0
+
+
+def single_layer_orbit_counter(
+    layer: int, generators: list[Counter[int]]
+) -> Counter[int]:
+    """Recover the standard Fibonacci-partition spectrum on one layer."""
+    if layer < 1 or layer >= len(generators):
+        raise ValueError("generator table must include costs through layer")
+    levels: Counter[int] = Counter({1: 1})
+    for cost in range(1, layer + 1):
+        orbit_weight = 2 if cost < layer else 1
+        for level, word_count in generators[cost].items():
+            levels[level] += orbit_weight * word_count
+    return levels
+

+\begin{abstract}
+Let \(R(n)\) be the number of partitions of \(n\) into distinct Fibonacci
+numbers, with the two unit terms identified.  On the standard Fibonacci layer
+\(\mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1)\), we determine the all-real moment

+deviation principle; the rate is affine on the coexistence interval.  The
+proof uses a weighted renewal identity for Weinstein's free generators,
+published Stern--Brocot denominator pressure, and a parity-free orbit-filling
+argument for the nonexposed slopes.

+\section{Thermodynamics of the Fibonacci partition function}
+\label{sec:standard-thermodynamics}
+
+The renewal identity was derived from Weinstein's standard Fibonacci
+partition function before it was transferred to the finite-window fold.  We
+now state its one-layer consequences intrinsically.  This removes the bespoke
+fold from the probabilistic conclusions.
+
+For \(m\ge1\), recall
+\[
+ \mathcal I_m=[F_{m+1}-1,F_{m+2}-1)
+\]
+and define
+\[
+ Z_m^R(t):=\sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^t
+ \qquad(t\in\RR).
+\]
+If \(\mathbf N_m\) is uniform on \(\mathcal I_m\), put
+\[
+ Y_m^R:=\frac1m\log R(\mathbf N_m).
+\]
+
+\begin{theorem}[One-layer Fibonacci partition thermodynamics]
+\label{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics}
+For every \(t\in\RR\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log Z_m^R(t)=P(t),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-pressure}
+\end{equation}
+where \(P\) is the pressure in \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure}.  Thus the
+one-layer pressure is zero on \((-\infty,-\sigma_0]\), is positive, real
+analytic, and strictly convex on \((-\sigma_0,\infty)\), and has the
+one-sided derivatives in \eqref{eq:critical-pressure-slopes}.
+
+For \(s>\sigma_0\), the unnormalized sums satisfy
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-s)\longrightarrow
+ \mathcal Z_R(s):=
+ \frac2{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-1.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-frozen-limit}
+\end{equation}
+At the critical tilt,
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)\sim\frac{2m}{\mu_C}.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}
+\end{equation}
+
+For \(n\in\mathcal I_m\) with \(R(n)>2\), let \(g(n)\) be the generating
+number of its Weinstein orbit and put \(\ell_m^R(n)=L(g(n))\); set
+\(\ell_m^R(n)=0\) when \(R(n)\le2\).  Let \(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m\) have the
+critical Gibbs law
+\[
+ \Pr\{\widehat{\mathbf N}_m=n\}
+ =\frac{R(n)^{-\sigma_0}}{Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)}
+ \qquad(n\in\mathcal I_m).
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}
+ \left(
+  \frac1m\log R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m),
+  \frac1m\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)
+ \right)
+ \xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{\mathrm d}(v_cU,U),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-gibbs}
+\end{equation}
+where \(U\) is uniform on \([0,1]\).
+
+Finally, \((Y_m^R)\) satisfies a full large deviation principle with speed
+\(m\) and the good rate function
+\begin{equation}
+ I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}
+ \{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-ldp-rate}
+\end{equation}
+Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), where
+\(\alpha_+=\tfrac12\log\varphi\), and
+\[
+ I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
+ \qquad(0\le\alpha\le v_c).
+\]
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put \(H_m(s)=\sum_{j=0}^m u_j(s)\).  The exact one-layer renewal identity
+\eqref{eq:weighted-layer-renewal} says
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-s)=2H_{m-1}(s)+u_m(s)-1.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-renewal}
+\end{equation}
+The proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} established
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log u_m(s)
+ =\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log H_m(s)
+ =P(-s).
+\]
+Since \(u_m(s)\le Z_m^R(-s)\le3H_m(s)\), this proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure}.
+
+If \(s>\sigma_0\), then \(U_s(1)=\sum_{j\ge0}u_j(s)<\infty\), so
+\(u_m(s)\to0\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-generating-function} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} give
+\[
+ U_s(1)=\frac1{1-B_s(1)}
+ =\frac1{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}.
+\]
+Letting \(m\to\infty\) in \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-frozen-limit}.  At \(s=\sigma_0\), the arithmetic
+renewal theorem used in \Cref{thm:critical-finite-window-gibbs} gives
+\(u_m(\sigma_0)\to1/\mu_C\).  Ces\`aro summation in
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}.
+
+We next retain the generating cost.  The four orbit branches displayed above
+\eqref{eq:marked-microcanonical-count} show that a generator of cost \(c\)
+contributes two points to \(\mathcal I_m\) if \(c<m\), one if \(c=m\), and
+none if \(c>m\).  Thus the one-layer boundary weight is
+\[
+ K_m^R(c)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  2,&c<m,\\
+  1,&c=m,\\
+  0,&c>m.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+With the marked renewal measure \(\mathcal U\) defined before
+\eqref{eq:marked-microcanonical-count}, the same free-monoid bijection gives,
+for every Borel set
+\(B\subset\mathbb R\times(\log2,\infty)\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \card{\{n\in\mathcal I_m:
+   (\ell_m^R(n),\log R(n))\in B\}}
+ =\int_B K_m^R(c)e^{\sigma_0h}\,\mathcal U(dc,dh).
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-marked-count}
+\end{equation}
+The points with \(R(n)\le2\) have bounded total critical weight, uniformly in
+\(m\), by the uniform layer-count lemma.
+
+For every bounded continuous \(f\) on \([0,1]\), the arithmetic renewal
+theorem and a Riemann-sum argument give
+\[
+ \frac1m\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_j(\sigma_0)f(j/m)
+ \longrightarrow\frac1{\mu_C}\int_0^1f(y)\,dy.
+\]
+After multiplication of \eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} by
+\(e^{-\sigma_0h}\), the weights are two for \(j<m\) and one at \(j=m\).
+Together with \eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}, this proves
+\[
+ \frac{\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)}m
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}U.
+\]
+For the reward coordinate, the critical renewal increments
+\((C_i,H_i)\) satisfy
+\[
+ \frac{H_1+\cdots+H_r}{C_1+\cdots+C_r}
+ \longrightarrow\frac{\mu_H}{\mu_C}=v_c
+\quad\text{almost surely}.
+\]
+Every cost increment is at least three.  Consequently the number of renewal
+epochs with total cost at most \(m\) and reward-to-cost ratio outside a fixed
+\(\delta\)-neighborhood of \(v_c\) is \(o(m)\), pathwise and, by bounded
+convergence after division by \(m\), in expectation.  Since \(K_m^R\le2\),
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} and
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size} imply
+\[
+ \frac1m\log R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)
+ -v_c\frac{\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)}m
+ \xrightarrow{\Pr}0.
+\]
+This proves \eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-gibbs}.
+
+It remains to prove the full LDP, in particular the lower bound at the
+nonexposed slopes.  The layer has
+\(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\), and hence
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log\card{\mathcal I_m}=\log\varphi.
+\]
+Equation \eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure} therefore gives the limiting
+logarithmic moment generating function
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m
+ \log\mathbb E e^{tmY_m^R}=P(t)-\log\varphi.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-log-mgf}
+\]
+The translated extremal theorem in the Fibonacci-convention lemma gives
+\[
+ \max_{n\in\mathcal I_m}\frac1m\log R(n)
+ \longrightarrow\alpha_+.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-maximum}
+\]
+Indeed, the two shifted endpoints have partition value one, so they do not
+change the maximum on the intervening Fibonacci block.  Thus the variables
+are exponentially tight, and the G\"artner--Ellis upper bound gives the
+required upper bound for closed sets.
+
+For the lower bound, fix \(t>t_c=-\sigma_0\), write \(v=P'(t)>v_c\), and
+tilt the uniform law on \(\mathcal I_n\) by \(R(k)^t\).  Analyticity of \(P\)
+and the exponential Markov inequality applied to
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure} show that this tilted law assigns
+exponentially vanishing mass to
+\[
+ \left\{k\in\mathcal I_n:
+   \left|n^{-1}\log R(k)-v\right|\ge\delta\right\}.
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ A_n^R(v,\delta)
+ :=\card{\{k\in\mathcal I_n:
+ |n^{-1}\log R(k)-v|<\delta\}},
+\]
+then
+\begin{equation}
+ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log A_n^R(v,\delta)
+ \ge P(t)-tv-|t|\delta.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}
+\end{equation}
+
+For large \(n\), every point counted here has multiplicity greater than two.
+Each generating orbit contributes at most two points to \(\mathcal I_n\).
+Keeping one generator from each represented orbit therefore produces a set
+\(\mathcal G_n^R\) with
+\[
+ \card{\mathcal G_n^R}\ge\tfrac12A_n^R(v,\delta),
+ \qquad L(g)\le n\quad(g\in\mathcal G_n^R),
+\]
+and \(n^{-1}\log R(g)\in(v-\delta,v+\delta)\).
+
+Fix \(0<\alpha<\alpha_+\), set \(\rho=\alpha/v<1\), and put
+\(n_m=\lfloor\rho m\rfloor\).  For \(g\in\mathcal G_{n_m}^R\), define
+\[
+ z_m(g)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  [a]g,&m-L(g)=2a,\\
+  [a]\tau g,&m-L(g)=2a+1.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+The orbit formulas give \(L(z_m(g))=m\) and
+\(R(z_m(g))=R(g)\), so \(z_m(g)\in\mathcal I_m\).  Freeness makes this map
+injective.  From \eqref{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}, first letting
+\(\delta\downarrow0\), we obtain the local counting lower bound
+\begin{equation}
+ \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac1m
+ \log A_m^R(\alpha,\varepsilon)
+ \ge\frac{\alpha}{v}\bigl(P(t)-tv\bigr).
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-orbit-filling}
+\end{equation}
+
+If \(0<\alpha\le v_c\), let \(t\downarrow t_c\) in
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-orbit-filling}; then \(v\downarrow v_c\) and the
+right side tends to \(\sigma_0\alpha\).  If
+\(v_c<\alpha<\alpha_+\), let \(t_\alpha\) be the unique point with
+\(P'(t_\alpha)=\alpha\), and let \(t\downarrow t_\alpha\) through values with
+\(P'(t)>\alpha\).  The right side then tends to
+\(P(t_\alpha)-t_\alpha\alpha\).  In both cases this is
+\(\log\varphi-I(\alpha)\).  Division by
+\(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\) proves the LDP lower bound at every interior
+point of the effective domain.
+
+The effective domain and the affine formula follow from the same convex-dual
+calculation as in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp}, since the pressure is the same.
+At \(0\), the left endpoint \(F_{m+1}-1\) has \(R=1\) and supplies the lower
+bound directly.  At \(\alpha_+\), use interior points tending to the endpoint
+and continuity of the finite convex rate on \([0,\alpha_+]\).  Hence the
+lower bound holds for every open set, completing the full LDP.
+\end{proof}

 Date of search: 2026-08-02 (Asia/Singapore).
 
+## Named-problem and standard-object audit (2026-08-14)
+
+The search was repeated against primary texts and four bibliographic
+services.  The arXiv Atom query 'all:"Fibonacci partition"' returned twelve
+records.  Crossref DOI records and zbMATH Open confirmed the publication
+metadata below.  Semantic Scholar's DOI endpoint returned Weinstein's
+six-item citation graph and the five-item citation graph of Chow--Slattery;
+its free-text endpoint and a later request for the 2022 paper returned HTTP
+429.  Exact-phrase arXiv and Crossref searches, the available citation
+graphs, and full-text checks of the later Fibonacci-partition papers located
+no resolution of the following three problems.  This is evidence of current
+status, not a claim of exhaustive priority.
+
+1. F. V. Weinstein, *Notes on Fibonacci Partitions*, Experimental
+   Mathematics 25 (2016), 482--499,
+   doi:10.1080/10586458.2015.1118416, p. 18:
+   **"How to describe the set of F-primitive numbers?"**
+
+   The paper's weighted-generator renewal
+   (prop:weighted-generator-renewal) and Tauberian law
+   (thm:psi-tauberian) enumerate Weinstein generators by multiplier and
+   cost.  They do not decide whether the *minimal integer* at a fixed
+   multiplier is f-simple.  The missing step is an order-sensitive
+   comparison excluding every non-simple orbit representative below the
+   least simple representative.
+
+2. Weinstein, ibid., Conjecture 9.1, pp. 19--20:
+   **"Then \(C_i\) coincides with the convex hull of the set of points
+   \((c,F(c))\)"** for the explicitly defined sets \(B_1(i)\), and also
+   \(B_2(i)\) in even layers.
+
+   The interval identity (thm:fiber-partition-interval) canonically
+   recovers every value of the standard function \(R=F\) on these layers,
+   and thm:unconditional-extremal-fibers proves the top horizontal support
+   value and all its maximizers.  The conjecture requires every supporting
+   slope.  What is missing is a uniform supporting-line inequality for all
+   partition values, not another maximum computation.
+
+3. F. V. Weinstein, *On a theorem of J. Shallit concerning Fibonacci
+   partitions*, Communications in Mathematics 30 (2022), 203--207,
+   doi:10.46298/cm.10769, Conjecture 3.3, p. 207:
+   **"\(r_3^{(a,i,b)}(n)-r_3^{(a,j,b)}(n)\le1\) for any
+   \(i,j\in\{0,1,2\}\). Moreover, [the product of the three pairwise
+   differences] \(=0\)."**
+
+   The coefficient-spectrum identity in thm:affine-transfer starts from
+   the same truncated product, and a part-count mark replaces it by
+   \(\prod_{r=a}^b(1+u z^{f_r})\).  The present Fourier formulas act on the
+   value coordinate only.  The missing input is a roots-of-unity
+   cancellation theorem at \(u^3=1\), uniform in \(a,b,n\); no such estimate
+   follows from the unmarked renewal.
+
+### Closed false lead
+
+Chow--Slattery, *On Fibonacci partitions*, J. Number Theory 225 (2021),
+310--326, Conjecture 1.4, asked whether
+**"\(B(H)\to B\) \((H\to\infty)\)"**.  This is not still open.  Zhou,
+*On the Representation Functions of Certain Numeration Systems*,
+arXiv:2305.00792, Corollary 1.5, explicitly states that its Fibonacci
+specialization solves Conjecture 1.4 and the first three problems on
+Chow--Slattery p. 315.  It is therefore excluded from the candidate list.
+
+### A/B/C/D decision
+
+- **(A):** The three live problems are genuine, but the manuscript lacks the
+  order-sensitive minimum comparison, all-slope support inequalities, and
+  roots-of-unity cancellation they respectively require.
+- **(B):** The exact identity
+  \(d_m(x)=R(\chi_m(x))\) maps the bespoke fibers bijectively to two standard
+  Fibonacci layers.  More strongly, the already proved generator renewal has
+  exact one-layer weights \(2,1\).  This route is selected.
+- **(C):** The main pressure and LDP are already unconditional.  The local
+  prime-support theorem stops at an active-cutoff stable/semistable renewal
+  input; the dyadic infinite-variance and no-positive-exponential-moment
+  calculation shows that this is a real obstruction, not a removable
+  Gaussian hypothesis.
+- **(D):** The largest-fiber formulas, freezing boundary, critical constants,
+  and LDP exponent are already sharp.  The compact-operator obstruction has
+  no plausible converse without specifying an operator class beyond the
+  hypotheses it rules out.
+
+The selected theorem is now thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics: all-real

+def critical_single_layer_partition(layer: int, renewal: list[float]) -> float:
+    """Evaluate the exact one-layer critical partition function from u_j."""
+    if layer < 1 or layer >= len(renewal):
+        raise ValueError("renewal coefficients must be available through layer")
+    return 2.0 * sum(renewal[:layer]) + renewal[layer] - 1.0
+
+
+def single_layer_orbit_counter(
+    layer: int, generators: list[Counter[int]]
+) -> Counter[int]:
+    """Recover the standard Fibonacci-partition spectrum on one layer."""
+    if layer < 1 or layer >= len(generators):
+        raise ValueError("generator table must include costs through layer")
+    levels: Counter[int] = Counter({1: 1})
+    for cost in range(1, layer + 1):
+        orbit_weight = 2 if cost < layer else 1
+        for level, word_count in generators[cost].items():
+            levels[level] += orbit_weight * word_count
+    return levels
+

+and define
+\[
+ Z_m^R(t):=\sum_{n\in\mathcal I_m}R(n)^t
+ \qquad(t\in\RR).
+\]
+If \(\mathbf N_m\) is uniform on \(\mathcal I_m\), put
+\[
+ Y_m^R:=\frac1m\log R(\mathbf N_m).
+\]
+
+\begin{theorem}[One-layer Fibonacci partition thermodynamics]
+\label{thm:standard-fibonacci-thermodynamics}
+For every \(t\in\RR\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log Z_m^R(t)=P(t),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-pressure}
+\end{equation}
+where \(P\) is the pressure in \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure}.  Thus the
+one-layer pressure is zero on \((-\infty,-\sigma_0]\), is positive, real
+analytic, and strictly convex on \((-\sigma_0,\infty)\), and has the
+one-sided derivatives in \eqref{eq:critical-pressure-slopes}.
+
+For \(s>\sigma_0\), the unnormalized sums satisfy
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-s)\longrightarrow
+ \mathcal Z_R(s):=
+ \frac2{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}-1.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-frozen-limit}
+\end{equation}
+At the critical tilt,
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)\sim\frac{2m}{\mu_C}.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}
+\end{equation}
+
+For \(n\in\mathcal I_m\) with \(R(n)>2\), let \(g(n)\) be the generating
+number of its Weinstein orbit and put \(\ell_m^R(n)=L(g(n))\); set
+\(\ell_m^R(n)=0\) when \(R(n)\le2\).  Let \(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m\) have the
+critical Gibbs law
+\[
+ \Pr\{\widehat{\mathbf N}_m=n\}
+ =\frac{R(n)^{-\sigma_0}}{Z_m^R(-\sigma_0)}
+ \qquad(n\in\mathcal I_m).
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}
+ \left(
+  \frac1m\log R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m),
+  \frac1m\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)
+ \right)
+ \xrightarrow[m\to\infty]{\mathrm d}(v_cU,U),
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-critical-gibbs}
+\end{equation}
+where \(U\) is uniform on \([0,1]\).
+
+Finally, \((Y_m^R)\) satisfies a full large deviation principle with speed
+\(m\) and the good rate function
+\begin{equation}
+ I(\alpha)=\sup_{t\in\RR}
+ \{t\alpha-P(t)+\log\varphi\}.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-ldp-rate}
+\end{equation}
+Its effective domain is \([0,\alpha_+]\), where
+\(\alpha_+=\tfrac12\log\varphi\), and
+\[
+ I(\alpha)=\log\varphi-\sigma_0\alpha
+ \qquad(0\le\alpha\le v_c).
+\]
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put \(H_m(s)=\sum_{j=0}^m u_j(s)\).  The exact one-layer renewal identity
+\eqref{eq:weighted-layer-renewal} says
+\begin{equation}
+ Z_m^R(-s)=2H_{m-1}(s)+u_m(s)-1.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-renewal}
+\end{equation}
+The proof of \Cref{thm:all-real-pressure} established
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log u_m(s)
+ =\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log H_m(s)
+ =P(-s).
+\]
+Since \(u_m(s)\le Z_m^R(-s)\le3H_m(s)\), this proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure}.
+
+If \(s>\sigma_0\), then \(U_s(1)=\sum_{j\ge0}u_j(s)<\infty\), so
+\(u_m(s)\to0\).  Equations
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-generating-function} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-renewal-at-one} give
+\[
+ U_s(1)=\frac1{1-B_s(1)}
+ =\frac1{2-\zeta(s-1)/\zeta(s)}.
+\]
+Letting \(m\to\infty\) in \eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-frozen-limit}.  At \(s=\sigma_0\), the arithmetic
+renewal theorem used in \Cref{thm:critical-finite-window-gibbs} gives
+\(u_m(\sigma_0)\to1/\mu_C\).  Ces\`aro summation in
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-renewal} proves
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}.
+
+We next retain the generating cost.  The four orbit branches displayed above
+\eqref{eq:marked-microcanonical-count} show that a generator of cost \(c\)
+contributes two points to \(\mathcal I_m\) if \(c<m\), one if \(c=m\), and
+none if \(c>m\).  Thus the one-layer boundary weight is
+\[
+ K_m^R(c)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  2,&c<m,\\
+  1,&c=m,\\
+  0,&c>m.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+With the marked renewal measure \(\mathcal U\) defined before
+\eqref{eq:marked-microcanonical-count}, the same free-monoid bijection gives,
+for every Borel set
+\(B\subset\mathbb R\times(\log2,\infty)\),
+\begin{equation}
+ \card{\{n\in\mathcal I_m:
+   (\ell_m^R(n),\log R(n))\in B\}}
+ =\int_B K_m^R(c)e^{\sigma_0h}\,\mathcal U(dc,dh).
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-marked-count}
+\end{equation}
+The points with \(R(n)\le2\) have bounded total critical weight, uniformly in
+\(m\), by the uniform layer-count lemma.
+
+For every bounded continuous \(f\) on \([0,1]\), the arithmetic renewal
+theorem and a Riemann-sum argument give
+\[
+ \frac1m\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}u_j(\sigma_0)f(j/m)
+ \longrightarrow\frac1{\mu_C}\int_0^1f(y)\,dy.
+\]
+After multiplication of \eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} by
+\(e^{-\sigma_0h}\), the weights are two for \(j<m\) and one at \(j=m\).
+Together with \eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size}, this proves
+\[
+ \frac{\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)}m
+ \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}U.
+\]
+For the reward coordinate, the critical renewal increments
+\((C_i,H_i)\) satisfy
+\[
+ \frac{H_1+\cdots+H_r}{C_1+\cdots+C_r}
+ \longrightarrow\frac{\mu_H}{\mu_C}=v_c
+\quad\text{almost surely}.
+\]
+Every cost increment is at least three.  Consequently the number of renewal
+epochs with total cost at most \(m\) and reward-to-cost ratio outside a fixed
+\(\delta\)-neighborhood of \(v_c\) is \(o(m)\), pathwise and, by bounded
+convergence after division by \(m\), in expectation.  Since \(K_m^R\le2\),
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-marked-count} and
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-size} imply
+\[
+ \frac1m\log R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)
+ -v_c\frac{\ell_m^R(\widehat{\mathbf N}_m)}m
+ \xrightarrow{\Pr}0.
+\]
+This proves \eqref{eq:standard-layer-critical-gibbs}.
+
+It remains to prove the full LDP, in particular the lower bound at the
+nonexposed slopes.  The layer has
+\(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\), and hence
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\log\card{\mathcal I_m}=\log\varphi.
+\]
+Equation \eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure} therefore gives the limiting
+logarithmic moment generating function
+\[
+ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m
+ \log\mathbb E e^{tmY_m^R}=P(t)-\log\varphi.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-log-mgf}
+\]
+The translated extremal theorem in the Fibonacci-convention lemma gives
+\[
+ \max_{n\in\mathcal I_m}\frac1m\log R(n)
+ \longrightarrow\alpha_+.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-maximum}
+\]
+Indeed, the two shifted endpoints have partition value one, so they do not
+change the maximum on the intervening Fibonacci block.  Thus the variables
+are exponentially tight, and the G\"artner--Ellis upper bound gives the
+required upper bound for closed sets.
+
+For the lower bound, fix \(t>t_c=-\sigma_0\), write \(v=P'(t)>v_c\), and
+tilt the uniform law on \(\mathcal I_n\) by \(R(k)^t\).  Analyticity of \(P\)
+and the exponential Markov inequality applied to
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-pressure} show that this tilted law assigns
+exponentially vanishing mass to
+\[
+ \left\{k\in\mathcal I_n:
+   \left|n^{-1}\log R(k)-v\right|\ge\delta\right\}.
+\]
+Consequently, if
+\[
+ A_n^R(v,\delta)
+ :=\card{\{k\in\mathcal I_n:
+ |n^{-1}\log R(k)-v|<\delta\}},
+\]
+then
+\begin{equation}
+ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log A_n^R(v,\delta)
+ \ge P(t)-tv-|t|\delta.
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}
+\end{equation}
+
+For large \(n\), every point counted here has multiplicity greater than two.
+Each generating orbit contributes at most two points to \(\mathcal I_n\).
+Keeping one generator from each represented orbit therefore produces a set
+\(\mathcal G_n^R\) with
+\[
+ \card{\mathcal G_n^R}\ge\tfrac12A_n^R(v,\delta),
+ \qquad L(g)\le n\quad(g\in\mathcal G_n^R),
+\]
+and \(n^{-1}\log R(g)\in(v-\delta,v+\delta)\).
+
+Fix \(0<\alpha<\alpha_+\), set \(\rho=\alpha/v<1\), and put
+\(n_m=\lfloor\rho m\rfloor\).  For \(g\in\mathcal G_{n_m}^R\), define
+\[
+ z_m(g)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  [a]g,&m-L(g)=2a,\\
+  [a]\tau g,&m-L(g)=2a+1.
+ \end{cases}
+\]
+The orbit formulas give \(L(z_m(g))=m\) and
+\(R(z_m(g))=R(g)\), so \(z_m(g)\in\mathcal I_m\).  Freeness makes this map
+injective.  From \eqref{eq:standard-layer-exposed-source}, first letting
+\(\delta\downarrow0\), we obtain the local counting lower bound
+\begin{equation}
+ \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\liminf_{m\to\infty}\frac1m
+ \log A_m^R(\alpha,\varepsilon)
+ \ge\frac{\alpha}{v}\bigl(P(t)-tv\bigr).
+ \label{eq:standard-layer-orbit-filling}
+\end{equation}
+
+If \(0<\alpha\le v_c\), let \(t\downarrow t_c\) in
+\eqref{eq:standard-layer-orbit-filling}; then \(v\downarrow v_c\) and the
+right side tends to \(\sigma_0\alpha\).  If
+\(v_c<\alpha<\alpha_+\), let \(t_\alpha\) be the unique point with
+\(P'(t_\alpha)=\alpha\), and let \(t\downarrow t_\alpha\) through values with
+\(P'(t)>\alpha\).  The right side then tends to
+\(P(t_\alpha)-t_\alpha\alpha\).  In both cases this is
+\(\log\varphi-I(\alpha)\).  Division by
+\(\card{\mathcal I_m}=F_m\) proves the LDP lower bound at every interior
+point of the effective domain.
+
+The effective domain and the affine formula follow from the same convex-dual
+calculation as in \Cref{thm:full-fiber-ldp}, since the pressure is the same.
+At \(0\), the left endpoint \(F_{m+1}-1\) has \(R=1\) and supplies the lower
+bound directly.  At \(\alpha_+\), use interior points tending to the endpoint
+and continuity of the finite convex rate on \([0,\alpha_+]\).  Hence the
+lower bound holds for every open set, completing the full LDP.
+\end{proof}
